As a sci-fi lover, Control was my fav supernatural game of all time.
The great physics, the mystery, graphics, lighting effects, level design, performance and the fluid movement. All of it is still here in Control Resonant. But sadly it's not as fun as it used to be and here is why.

The protagonist
Compared to Jesse, Dylan feels underwhelming. he is fragile, lifeless, bossed around and shy. his facial expressions and body shape are unthreatening. his pose is weak and gives me powerless vibes. His personality is not only not fitting his role as a dangerous super hero in a world where sharpness and seriousness aren't just recommended, it's required — Dylan character kills the energy in the game.

Gameplay
Given the game's era, when I first saw the trailers I was surprised that they decided to go with melee as the main weapon, but I thought why not, it would be an interesting new experience. Now I see that melee feels less efficient and less impactful and it change how you play the game since you have to dash or run to each enemy. It's not as fun as the first game and takes away from the sci-fi feeling.

Verdict
The game is not necessarily bad, some might like it even more than the first game. For me personally, what made me love Control the most isn't here anymore. Confidence and boldness included.

Remedy really crafted a beauty of a game. The level design in this game is phenomenal and trippy as fuck(In a good way). The amount of detail they display for the Manhattan they created is astounding. Just take a look around an you'll see what I mean. The flow of the story is also well done, and it does a great job of making you want to know more. Even the side story quests have great narratives as well. One of the best parts of this game is Zoe's mixtape. The curated playlist is fantastic, and whenever a song is played it fits the vibe of what's going on in the story. I also want to highlight Dylan and Zoe's relationship in this game. They work so well with each other, and seeing their growth from the beginning of the game is really endearing. The combat in this game is fun and well done, but you can definitely tell it's Remedy's first time making a melee action game. It's good but it's not the most in-depth combat out there, which is completely fine, they'll only get better. Overall this is my GOTY and I don't see it changing. I 100% recommend this game at it's full price!

The clarity of the combat is a complete shambles. The camera distance and the sheer amount of action make the attacks difficult to follow. Attacks from enemies off-screen, signalled by a faint yellow banner when the screen is already cluttered with overlapping information, are not effective.

Control 1 could retaliate this by being a shooter. A character-action hack’n slash doesn’t forgive this.

Though, the game runs really well. The story, music and level design are beautiful. It’s quite polished.

Agora, isso faz o jogo deixar de ser uma masterpiece? Eu acho que não. O que a Remedy consegue fazer nesse jogo, divisivo, claro, mas consistentemente disruptivo e tentando fazer algo novo nesse gênero (que lembrando, ele é estreante) tão saturado. Conceitos convencionais como POIs e Side Quests funcionam de um jeito que você esperaria em algum da Ubisoft, agora, sempre tem alguma coisinha que é nova, refrescante, mesmo que eu não fosse tão fã, era audacioso, corajoso e, porra cara, isso é algo que merece ser pontuado. Um jogo conseguir uma vez atrás da outra se desafiar e desafiar o jogador a se experimentar é muito gostoso de estar experienciando.

E é meio que isso, isso é o que eu acho tão fantástico nesse jogo — o que a Remedy fez em Alan Wake II — pegar um gênero que você conhece muito, muito bem e mesmo assim te colocar em uma perspectiva completamente nova, desconhecida. Enfim, eu genuinamente recomendo, é um dos melhores desse ano definitivamente.

I don't think this needed to be like DMC by any means, but after a while I adjusted some settings to speed up the combat and downloaded a mod that allows you to swap weapons and finishers while fighting that helped to lessen these issues.

The story is pretty great but the combat just bores the shit out of me. I've not finished the game yet and idk if I will at this rate. If you're here for fun gunplay or melee like the first game you're a bit out of luck imo. The best part of Resonant is by far the story and lore. Outside of that though, it's lacking compared to the first Control game.

It lacks the charm of The Oldest House, the weirdness of the Darling video logs, and the intrigue of each new discovered area. I never felt out of my element in Resonant. Nothing felt truly unthinkable or new unlike the often literally twisting halls of The Oldest House.

I didn't much care for the boss fights either. Most bosses would just spam one or two moves and that'd be it. Very little variance, very large health pools. The healing system is also generally miserable. You're either full health or at 10%. I often found myself in a situation where if I got low on HP there was little room for recovery but when I was high HP there was little risk to any given encounter.

Resonant is a cool game with mediocre combat and interesting but unimpressive environments. I wanted so desperately to love this game the way I did the first one but I just... don't.

I was a bit worried that Resonant would end up being more of a side show than a fully fleshed-out Remedy game, but wow was that unfounded. The game is incredibly well-rounded, combat is satisfying, character building is engaging, and they do some very interesting things with world traversal. In general, the devs have made some bold choices which worse management might've told them the gaming market was not ready for. The result is a game that absolutely stands on its own while still being a meaningful entry into the Remedyverse. Its lore, narrative and story is a joy to experience, I was fully immersed in it. Relating to the protagonist Dylan took me a moment, but once I understood what he was all about, I absolutely loved him. Great writing, great gameplay, a must play!

New Gameplay style from Remedy and oh man. IT DID NOT DISAPPOINT. The story, the environment, the side missions were all fun. Truly a unique experience, Remedy really crafted a masterpiece and I can't wait for their next game. GET THIS GAME.

Once again, I have completed the Finnish national responsibility/pleasure of playing a Remedy game on release. No other AAA studio dares to swing for the fences like Remedy and I couldn't be prouder. For me the things I'm most proud of as a Finn, are Fazerin Sininen, Sasha Barkov and Remedy. 

Even though the combat could have used an additional layer of depth, especially considering the significant length of the game and the amount of things to do, I enjoyed every other aspect tremendously. Great OST, intriguing worldbuilding, actually interesting voice memos, notes and videos, the sheer visual spectacle of it all. The quest "Recursions and Iterations" will go in my pantheon of my favourite video game missions. This was a wonderful experience, and I can't wait to see what's next for Remedy, since this game really seems to be a well-deserved hit.

An entirely new combat system and it is somehow still just as vapid as the first game's. Really thought they were going to lean into the character action to make up for the lack of combat depth in the first CONTROL, but no, its extremely button mashy against tanky enemies with almost no combo variety.

Also, CONTROL's best part, the setting, is now completely botched. The bleak and confusing level design of The Oldest House works by creating the illusion of a space that sprawling, mysterious, and alive. The bleak and confusing level design applied to the city of New York just makes me bored and lost. The most interesting moments of discovery were never made on my own, it was in railroaded sections where the game locks you down and says 'HEY LOOK AT THIS'.

In terms of plot, the intro hours are very strong, but quality falls off a cliff. The game has a recurring problem of violating the classic arc of (Setup >> Build-Up >> Payoff). Every quest I interacted with had a serious problem of Setting Up well, but having no Build-Up and skipping straight to the Payoff. It makes every quest feel weirdly unsatisfying.

Also this game is plagued with AAA radio-comm dialogue, where you have a partner character constantly yapping in your ear. Its so bad, I thought it was satirical at first.

In an ocean of remakes, sequels, and “safe” games, Control Resonance bulldozes onto the scene like a completely unhinged acid trip and I mean that as a compliment.

It’s an action-heavy hack-and-slash wrapped around some genuinely intricate storytelling, especially once you start connecting the dots between this game and Remedy’s other games/universe. It throws you into open-zone exploration where the level design becomes so warped that you genuinely start questioning what counts as the floor, wall, or ceiling anymore.

Seriously, this game needs a warning: do not play drunk. You will get lost. You may never return.

The combat is fast, satisfying, and chaotic without completely overwhelming you. The environmental storytelling is fantastic, and the sound design deserves special recognition.

The biggest weakness is the pacing. It starts fairly slow and takes some time to really show you what kind of game it wants to be, but once it gets going, it REALLY gets going.

There aren’t many games willing to get this weird anymore, and Control Resonance deserves credit for actually taking some risks.

- Combat: 8/10
- Story: Epic/10
- Environmental storytelling: 10/10
- Pacing: 6/10 — slow start, then it ramps up
- Level design: Acid Trip/10
- Sound design: Give whoever was in charge of this a raise/10

Overall: 8.9/10

tldr.text: Very Positive (93%): players love the story, characters and challenging gameplay.
Gameplay and combat draw the most complaints, raised in 17% of reviews.

details.text: Recent reviews are about as positive as the all-time score, and crash complaints eased slightly, though some still cite "game-breaking crashes".
Players in their first hours are far less positive than long-time players, 66% against 97%, so the early hours matter most to anyone buying now.
